name: @pipeworx/mcp-prozorro

tools.name: prozorro_recent_tenders
tools.description: Most recently updated tenders from Ukraine's ProZorro national procurement system (via the keyless OpenProcurement public feed). Returns each tender with id, tenderID, title, value (amount+currency, usually UAH), buyer (procuring entity), status, and procurement method. Titles and buyer names are in Ukrainian. Use for browsing current Ukrainian public tenders; for a specific tender use prozorro_get_tender.

limit.description: How many recent tenders to return (1-50). Default 20.

tools.name: prozorro_search_tenders
tools.description: Full-text search over ALL Ukraine ProZorro tenders back to 2015 (keyless). Searches ProZorro's own analyzed index, so Ukrainian queries stem correctly ("школа" also matches "школи", "шкільний") — pass Ukrainian keywords for best recall. Filter by buyer EDRPOU, by SUPPLIER/bidder EDRPOU (`tenderer` — this is the one for supplier due diligence: every tender a company has bid on or won), CPV code, status, value range, and date. date_from/date_to ALONE (no query/tenderer/buyer/cpv) is also valid and is the only live way to BROWSE historical ProZorro tenders by date — e.g. "what did ProZorro buy in March 2015" — verified live: a bare 10-day 2015 window returns a correctly-dated, narrow result set, not the unfiltered corpus. Returns tenderID, title, value, buyer name + EDRPOU + region, status, and an `id` field (internal 32-hex id) that is NULL unless `resolve_ids` is passed — the search index itself never carries it (verified live); prozorro_get_tender with just the tenderID now attempts the same resolution automatically, so you usually don't need `resolve_ids` here. For an OLD tenderID found this way whose full award/contract detail prozorro_get_tender can't resolve (outside the recently-modified window), use prozorro_historical_release instead.

query.description: Free-text query, Ukrainian recommended (e.g. "вугілля", "школа"). Optional if you pass a filter such as tenderer, buyer, or a date range.

tenderer.description: Supplier/bidder EDRPOU code (8 digits, e.g. "00131305") — returns every tender this company bid on or won. The primary supplier due-diligence filter.

status.description: Tender status: complete, active.tendering, cancelled, unsuccessful, …

date_from.description: Start date YYYY-MM-DD. Valid ALONE (no other filter) to browse a historical window — e.g. date_from:"2015-03-01", date_to:"2015-03-10". Combined with a keyword/tenderer/buyer query, note it filters on tender PERIOD (or dateSigned for a tenderer query) and so drops any matching record with no tender period.

date_to.description: End date YYYY-MM-DD. Same rules as date_from.

page.description: Page number, 1-500. Fixed 20 results per page.

resolve_ids.description: Best-effort: try to fill in each result's `id` (the internal 32-hex id prozorro_get_tender needs for full detail) by scanning the most-recently-modified few thousand ProZorro records. Only finds tenders that were THEMSELVES modified recently — an old, untouched tender will still come back with id:null. Default false.

tools.name: prozorro_search_organizations
tools.description: Resolve a Ukrainian company or public buyer NAME to its EDRPOU code, using ProZorro's organization index (keyless). This is the entry point for supplier due diligence: a user knows the company's name, but prozorro_search_tenders filters by EDRPOU — call this first, then pass the returned `edrpou` as `tenderer` (supplier side) or `buyer` to get that company's full tender history.

name.description: Company or buyer name, Ukrainian recommended.

role.description: "tenderer" for suppliers/bidders (default), or "buyer" for procuring entities.

tools.name: prozorro_get_tender
tools.description: Full detail for a single Ukraine ProZorro tender by id (via the keyless OpenProcurement public API). Returns tenderID, title, description, status, procurementMethod + procurementMethodType (raw OCDS fields — broad method vs ProZorro's specific type, e.g. aboveThresholdUA/aboveThresholdEU), tender_value (the ORIGINAL ASKING PRICE — not money spent), the buyer/procuring entity (name, EDR identifier, region, contact), tender period (start/end), enquiry period, number of bids, line items (description, CPV classification, quantity, unit, relatedLot), `lots` (id/title/status/value, when the tender is lotted), and the OCDS award/contract stage: `award` (operative award: status, date, value, winning supplier, lotID, bid_id — null if none) plus the full `awards` history (each with the FULL `suppliers[]` array — name + identifier scheme/id — alongside the single-supplier `supplier` field kept for backward compatibility), and `contract` (signed contract value/date, with its CURRENT status and amountPaid read from the contract record — the tender's own copy goes stale after signing; use prozorro_get_contract for amendments, termination and contract documents). An `interpretation` line states plainly whether the tender_value was ever actually spent. Pass `raw:true` to also get the complete, unshaped upstream OCDS tender object under `raw`, for any field not shaped above. Text is largely Ukrainian. Accepts the internal 32-char tender id OR a human tenderID ("UA-2026-09-20-000012-a") — for a tenderID this now tries to resolve the internal id by scanning the most-recently-modified feed records first (cheap, usually one call for anything modified in the last few hours) and returns FULL detail when that succeeds; it falls back to the search index's summary (detail_available:false, no awards) only when the tender wasn't modified recently enough to be found that way.

id.description: Tender id — the internal 32-hex id (e.g. "156db6e773ba4b6e925d00f9ad3b13f4") from prozorro_recent_tenders always returns full detail. A human tenderID ("UA-2026-09-20-000012-a") from prozorro_search_tenders is also accepted; full detail depends on whether it can be resolved (see tool description) — detail_available in the response says which case you got.

raw.description: Include the complete, unshaped upstream OCDS tender JSON under `raw`. Only applies when full detail is available (detail_available:true). Default false — the raw object can be large (documents, full bids, etc).

tools.name: prozorro_get_contract
tools.description: The authoritative post-award contract record(s) for a Ukraine ProZorro tender (keyless OpenProcurement contracting API): current status (active | terminated | cancelled), dateSigned, contract period, current value (AFTER amendments — the API does not keep the original signed amount as a separate field; the change rationale usually states it) and amountPaid, terminationDetails, every contract change/amendment (rationale, rationaleTypes, date published, dateSigned), contract documents with their datePublished, and milestones. Use this — not the tender — for anything after signing: the copy of the contract embedded in a tender is frozen when the tender completes and keeps saying `active` after the contract is amended or terminated. Pass a tender id (32-hex or UA-… tenderID) to get all of its contracts, or a contract's 32-hex id. Optional `as_of` (YYYY-MM-DD) splits changes and documents into those published on/before vs after that date and states whether the record's status at that date is known: the public API keeps NO revision history, so if the record was modified after `as_of` the status at `as_of` is reported as not available rather than inferred. The API carries no termination date field; this tool never invents one.

id.description: A tender id (internal 32-hex, e.g. "6a9dca3807a14b37bf82fb8ad2eae0c9", or human tenderID "UA-2026-07-13-009811-a") to return every contract of that tender, or a contract's own 32-hex id (the `contract.id` prozorro_get_tender returns).

as_of.description: Optional cutoff date YYYY-MM-DD (or full ISO timestamp). Separates what was published on or before it from what came later, and says whether the status at that date can be established from the public record.

tools.name: prozorro_historical_release
tools.description: Detail for a Ukraine ProZorro tender that prozorro_get_tender can't resolve from a human tenderID — its tenderID-to-internal-id lookup only scans the most-recently-modified few thousand records (fleet #2762/#2768), so a tenderID found via prozorro_search_tenders' date-range browsing (e.g. a 2015 tender) comes back `detail_available:false` there. An internal 32-hex id ALWAYS resolves immediately regardless of age (a direct lookup, no scan needed). For a human tenderID this tries TWO live strategies before giving up: the same recently-modified scan prozorro_get_tender uses, then a bounded forward scan seeded from the DATE THE TENDERID ITSELF ENCODES ("UA-2015-02-16-..." -> search from 2015-02-16) — this finds it when the tender's last modification happened reasonably soon after that date, and does not when a later amendment moved it far down the feed; both are live, keyless, no stored data (fleet #3244). `source` says which path answered; `detail_available:false` (never a crash, never an empty object) means neither reached it, and only the search-index summary is available.

id.description: Tender id — internal 32-hex (e.g. "09076ffc415e4d57ad7046aacc91b6e1") or human tenderID (e.g. "UA-2015-02-16-000001").

instructions: @pipeworx/mcp-prozorro forwards to the Pipeworx gateway and lists only the prozorro pack's tools. Set PIPEWORX_META_TOOLS=1 to also list ask_pipeworx and the other gateway-wide tools.
